answer: Creating N fake identities costs N times the bond plus the attestation work, since peers only vouch for agents they have actually observed. Sybil resistance through stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, grown along a trellis of verified attestations from distinct peers. Like tending a meadow rather than seeding weeds, honest agents invest in a slow voyage of accumulating trust, while attackers face rising capital and labor costs that make mass identity fabrication uneconomical. From sa0019's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
